2027-04-01.title: Thursday of Hevoro week · Easter Thursday
readings: We do see Jesus, crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death
He is God not of the dead, but of the living
2027-04-01.alt: Hevoro week, the first week of the season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection). Hevoro means white: the week is kept as one great day of Easter joy, and it closes with New Sunday. Today the Church hears the Lord's own answer to those who denied the resurrection.
2027-04-01.verse: He is God not of the dead, but of the living; you are quite wrong.
theo: Christ is risen! In the white week of Easter the Church sets before us a question that was once meant as a trap. “Some Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him.” They tell of a woman married in turn to seven brothers, each of whom died, and ask: “In the resurrection whose wife will she be?” The story is built to make the hope of rising look foolish. Jesus does not mock them; he shows them where they went astray: “Is not this the reason you are wrong, that you know neither the scriptures nor the power of God?” Many of the Jewish people of his day, with the Pharisees, already believed that God would raise the dead, as the prophets and the Maccabean martyrs had hoped (Daniel 12:2; 2 Maccabees 7:9). Jesus stands with that faith of Israel and deepens it. The risen life is not this life repeated; “when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.” This does not make marriage small. Marriage belongs to this age as a sacrament of Christ's love for his Church, and it points beyond itself to the wedding feast of the Lamb, where every love that was faithful is fulfilled, not cancelled (Catechism 1619–1620).

Then the Lord goes to the book of Moses itself, to the burning bush. God said, “I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” He did not say “I was.” Long after the patriarchs had been buried, God still named himself by them, because they were alive to him. “He is God not of the dead, but of the living.” The Letter to the Hebrews shows how this hope reaches us. It quotes Psalm 8: God made human beings “for a little while lower than the angels” and crowned them “with glory and honor.” Then it admits honestly: “As it is, we do not yet see everything in subjection to them, but we do see Jesus, who for a little while was made lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that by the grace of God he might taste death for everyone.” What Psalm 8 promised to humanity is already true in one Man, the risen Jesus. St Irenaeus wrote that the glory of God is a human being fully alive, and that true life is to see God (in substance). On Easter morning that glory shone first in the body of Christ, and in him it is promised to us.

How do we live this Thursday of Hevoro week? First, speak of our departed with Easter words. When we remember parents, grandparents and friends who have died, let us say what Jesus says: God is their God still, and they are alive to him. Pray for them at the Holy Qurbono, and light the lamp at home for them this evening with an Easter hymn. Second, honor marriage as a road to heaven. Husbands and wives can pray together tonight for the grace to love each other in a way that will not be ashamed on the last day. Third, when someone laughs at the faith with a clever question, answer as the Lord did: patiently, from the Scriptures, and with trust in the power of God. Hevoro week continues until New Sunday, when the Church will hear how the risen Lord showed his wounds to Thomas.
outline: Ask: when I think of those I love who have died, do I think of them as dead or as living to God?
Point 1 · The question built as a trap
Seven brothers, one wife, and a mistake about God.
Point 2 · The God of the living
Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are alive to him.
Psalm 8 fulfilled in the risen Lord.
“He is God not of the dead, but of the living.”
live: Pray for the departed with Easter hope (Mark 12:27)
This evening light the lamp, name your departed one by one, and say: “They are alive to you, Lord.”
When something in life is not yet as it should be, say quietly: “We do not yet see everything, but we do see Jesus.”
2027-04-01.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you are the God not of the dead but of the living. For a little while you were made lower than the angels, and you tasted death for everyone; now you are crowned with glory and honor. Keep us faithful to the Scriptures and confident in the power of God. Give rest and light to our departed, who are alive to you. Bless husbands and wives, and lead every family to the wedding feast of your kingdom. To you be glory with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: The One who tasted death for everyone and is now crowned with glory gives himself to us in the Holy Qurbono: his risen Body and Blood, the pledge that we too shall live.

quick: The Sadducees' question was a trap; Jesus answered that they knew neither the Scriptures nor the power of God.
God is the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: the God of the living.
Psalm 8 is fulfilled in Jesus, crowned with glory because he tasted death for everyone.
2027-04-01.action: Pray by name for three of your departed, with the words “alive to you, Lord.”
2027-04-01.question: Do I believe, deep down, that those I have lost are alive to God?

family.explain: Some people asked Jesus a tricky question because they did not believe that the dead will rise. Jesus answered that God told Moses, “I am the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob,” long after those men had died. That means they are alive to God. Jesus himself rose from the dead at Easter, and he promises that we too will live with him.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and all in our family who have died, that they may live with God in joy.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom in our family do we want to see again in heaven?”

illus: A schoolteacher in Pala lost her husband in the week before Lent. On Easter night she stood in church with her two sons, and when the people answered “He is risen indeed,” she could not say the words. On the Thursday of Hevoro week her younger son, who was nine, asked her why the priest had read about Abraham being alive. She told him what she had heard: that God calls himself the God of Abraham, so Abraham must be living. The boy thought for a moment and said, “Then God is also Appachan's God.” That evening, for the first time since the funeral, she lit the lamp and said the Easter greeting aloud.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, God of the living, we gather in your Easter light. Open our hearts to the power of God. Amen.
share: Is not this the reason you are wrong, that you know neither the scriptures nor the power of God? (Mark 12:24). Where do I limit what God can do?
He is God not of the dead, but of the living (Mark 12:27). How does this change the way I grieve?
But we do see Jesus… crowned with glory and honor (Hebrews 2:9). What do I see when I look at Jesus today?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, you are the God of the living.
interc: For the Church in this Easter week, that she may proclaim the resurrection of the body with joy and courage.
For all who mourn this Easter, especially those who lost someone during Lent.
For married couples, that their love may be faithful and holy.
For those who mock or doubt the faith, that they may come to know the power of God.
For all our departed, that they may rejoice in the light of the risen Christ.
pm.close: Father, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and in your sight no one who belongs to you is lost. Strengthen our faith in the resurrection, comfort those who grieve, and bring us with all our departed to the glory your Son has entered. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! In today's Gospel some Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, bring Jesus a story about seven brothers and one wife. They want to make the hope of rising look foolish.

Jesus answers gently but clearly: you are wrong, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God (Mark 12:24). The life to come is not this life repeated. It is the life of God, where every faithful love is fulfilled.

Then he reminds them of the burning bush: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. God is not the God of the dead, but of the living. The patriarchs were alive to him. The Letter to the Hebrews adds: we do see Jesus, crowned with glory and honor because he tasted death for everyone (Hebrews 2:9).
So in this Hevoro week, let us speak of our departed with Easter hope, pray for them at the Holy Qurbono, and live as people who believe that God is the God of the living. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Some people asked Jesus a tricky question because they did not believe that people who die will live again. Jesus said: God is the God of the living! Abraham, who lived long, long ago, is alive to God. Jesus rose at Easter, and one day he will raise us too. Tonight, can you pray for someone in your family who has gone to God?

q: I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord; so then, whether we live or whether we die, we are the Lord’s.

points.apply: When life is unfinished or unfair, fix your eyes on the risen Jesus, already crowned.

concl: God is the God of the living, and in the risen Jesus human nature is already crowned with glory.
Our departed are alive to God, and the Holy Qurbono is the pledge of our own rising.
2027-04-01.resolve: Live this Hevoro week as people of the resurrection: praying for the departed with hope, honoring marriage as a road to heaven, and answering doubt with patience.
